title: House fire and horseback prosperity
odia:
ଘର ପୋଡିରୁ ବିପତ୍ତି ନାଇଁ
ଘୋଡ଼ା ଚଢ଼ାରୁ ସମ୍ପତ୍ତି ନାଇଁ।
literal_meaning: No calamity is greater than a house fire; no prosperity is greater than riding a horse.
meaning_odia: ଘର ପୋଡ଼ିଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ ବିପତ୍ତି ନାହିଁ, ଘୋଡ଼ା ଚଢ଼ାଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ ସମ୍ପତ୍ତି ନାହିଁ—ଏପରି ଅତିଶୟ ତୁଳନା କଥାଟି କରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଛବି ବଡ଼ କ୍ଷତିର, ଅନ୍ୟଟି ସମୃଦ୍ଧିର। ଦୁଇ ବିପରୀତ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ମନରେ ଗାଢ଼ କରିବା ଏହାର ଢଙ୍ଗ।
explanation: The saying places a burning home and a mounted rider at opposite ends of fortune. Its comparative wording presents each as unsurpassed: one in calamity, the other in prosperity. Our editorial reading treats those extremes as proverbial emphasis rather than a literal ranking of every possible loss or kind of wealth.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A discussion of the verse contrasts losing the security of home with a conspicuous image of prosperity. Readers notice how the two lines compress those extremes into memorable pictures.
cultural_context: ବିପତ୍ତି and ସମ୍ପତ୍ତି rhyme while naming opposite conditions. The matching negative endings intensify each comparison: nothing exceeds this. Horse riding serves as the saying’s chosen image of prosperity, paired with the destruction of a home.
